acceptance: make pr-rerun on a run whose only failure is a would-block duration verdict re-runs the fast-tier shards, so the verdict is computed from newly measured timings.
A regression test shows a failed-jobs-only rerun is not selected for that case, and that other failure kinds keep failed-jobs-only reruns.
pr-arm's would-block refusal names the rerun remedy alongside the baseline remedy.
context:
New occurrence on a Theseus re-lock PR (BenchBox #4059, head 3533b3c2ae49): core failed verify-fast-duration with sum ratio 1.395 (delta +669.9 s) on a runner whose calibration best was 0.900 s (speed factor 1.618). make pr-rerun re-ran only after the run completed, and the failed job re-failed on its first re-run. Re-running the single `test (ubuntu-latest, 3.14)` job with `gh run rerun --job` produced a passing verdict with no code change. The change touched only the lock and two workflow pin lines, so the slowdown was runner variance.

2026-11-11 further evidence from a retrospective over 25 sessions: delegated prompts gave contradictory recovery for a `verify-fast-duration` would-block. One said to run `make pr-rerun PR=<n>` first; three later ones said to rebase onto origin/develop and force-push with lease and never re-run. In one case a failed-jobs rerun reproduced a 1.522 ratio against the 1.30 limit, a full rerun passed, and the PR merged about 35 minutes later. docs/agent/merge-authority.md names only `make pr-rerun`; no document says when to rebase instead, or that repeating an unchanged rerun does not clear a would-block.

Revalidated 2026-11-11: still required. On origin/develop (c7b75c80bc) scripts/pr_rerun.py rerun_arguments (lines 204-220) returns `gh run rerun --failed` for any failed run and the full-run rerun only for cancelled runs; nothing inspects the duration verdict. scripts/pr_arm.py duration_verdict_refusals (lines 204-230) still offers only 'remove the slowdown, or regenerate the baseline' for would-block. docs/agent/merge-authority.md (lines ~222-235) still names only make pr-rerun and does not say when to rebase instead or that an unchanged failed-jobs rerun does not clear a would-block. Description corrected: the cited item ci-fast-duration-gate-slow-runner-margin-20261101 was merged into fast-duration-gate-calibration-skew-20261028, the open item for the gate-side fix; this item covers only the pr-rerun / pr-arm / docs side. Open PR #4120 (feature-pr-landing-guards-20261111) edits pr_arm.py and merge-authority.md; implement after it merges to avoid conflicts. Add to acceptance when implemented: docs/agent/merge-authority.md states that a would-block is cleared by a full re-run and when a rebase is the right remedy. Priority unchanged.
description:
Problem. The fast-tier duration gate in the core job can report would-block from slow-runner noise alone (tracked in fast-duration-gate-calibration-skew-20261028, which absorbed ci-fast-duration-gate-slow-runner-margin-20261101). The remedy is fresh timings, but make pr-rerun (scripts/pr_rerun.py rerun_arguments) re-runs only failed jobs of a failed run. The fast-tier shards passed, so only the core aggregate re-runs, and it re-reads the saved fast-junit artifact and reproduces the identical verdict. Observed on #4002 (a PR that only deletes tests): summed ratio 1.313, delta +442.6 s, median per-test ratio 1.010 on attempt 1, and exactly 1.313 again on the failed-jobs rerun (attempt 2). A full `gh run rerun` of the same run (attempt 3) measured 1.155 and passed. pr-arm's refusal text offers only 'remove the slowdown, or regenerate the baseline', neither of which applies to runner noise.

Change. When the only failure is a would-block duration verdict, make pr-rerun re-run the whole CI run (or the fast-tier shards plus core) so new timings are measured, and pr-arm's refusal names that remedy. A real slowdown must still block after the fresh measurement.
